name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
description: New Zealand's famous one-day volcanic hike: across craters, past the Emerald Lakes and down through tussock and forest. Distances are approximate.

mangatepopo.name: Mangatepopo Road End
mangatepopo.text: An old lava valley, boardwalks over the tussock, and the cone of Ngauruhoe ahead.

soda-springs.name: Soda Springs
soda-springs.text: The last easy water. Above, the Devil's Staircase climbs to the saddle.

south-crater.name: South Crater
south-crater.text: A flat, silent crater floor. Ngauruhoe towers to your left.

red-crater.name: Red Crater
red-crater.text: The highest point of the crossing. Steam, sulphur and rust-red walls.

emerald-lakes.name: Emerald Lakes
emerald-lakes.text: Three bright green pools at the foot of a scree slope.

blue-lake.name: Blue Lake
blue-lake.text: A cold crater lake, sacred to local Māori.

ketetahi-shelter.name: Ketetahi Shelter
ketetahi-shelter.text: A day shelter with a view over Lake Rotoaira and Taupō.

ketetahi-end.name: Ketetahi Road End
ketetahi-end.text: Down through the forest to the road. You crossed a volcano!

story.staircase: The Devil's Staircase: step after step of old lava. You stop to breathe and the valley is already small.
story.wind: On the ridge the wind pushes hard. You lean into it and keep your eyes on the marker poles.
story.scree: You slide down the loose scree in big, careful steps, and the lakes flash green below.
story.forest: The tussock gives way to trees. After hours of rock, the forest smells unbelievably green.

facts.gift: In 1887 Te Heuheu Tūkino IV, paramount chief of Ngāti Tūwharetoa, gifted these sacred peaks to the nation. The gift became the core of New Zealand's first national park.
facts.heritage: Tongariro is a dual World Heritage site, listed for nature in 1990 and in 1993 as the first site recognised as a cultural landscape.
facts.summits: The summits are tapu (sacred) to Ngāti Tūwharetoa. They ask walkers to enjoy the peaks from the track rather than climb to the top.
facts.film: Ngauruhoe, the near-perfect cone beside the track, stood in for a fictional volcano in a famous fantasy film trilogy. It last erupted in 1975.
facts.emerald: The Emerald Lakes get their colour from minerals washed out of the surrounding volcanic rock.
facts.blue-lake: Blue Lake is tapu: visitors are asked not to swim in it or eat and drink beside it.
facts.te-maari: In 2012 the Te Māri craters just north of the track erupted and threw rocks as far as the old Ketetahi Hut, which no longer takes overnight guests.

steam.name: Full Steam
steam.description: Walk 15 km in a single day.
